job.programs_hint: One program per tool, run them in this order. Each program first moves to the tool change position (X0 Y0, high up) and pauses with the spindle off: insert the tool, set Z0 to the panel surface and resume the program in your control software. At the end it parks at the same position.

tools.heading: Tool library
tools.lead: Drill bits and end mills the G-code is made for. A hole gets the drill of the same diameter; larger holes are milled with the end mill. Cutting values are starting values, tune them on your mill.
sim.title: 3D simulation of the drill and mill paths
sim.hint: Drag to turn the view, drag with the middle mouse button to move it, mouse wheel or the buttons to zoom. With the view in focus: arrow keys turn, + and - zoom, space starts and stops.
sim.load_failed: The programs could not be loaded.
sim.aria: 3D view of the panel with the tool paths

sim.note: The time is estimated from the feed rates of the programs; rapid moves are assumed at {rapid} mm/min. The depth is exaggerated so that it can be seen. Dark lines show where material is cut away.
machines.heading: Machines
machines.lead: Parameters of the printers and mills the files are made for. Calibration values can be changed for a single job under Settings on the New job page.
machines.m_offset: Panel position on the machine (X, Y)
settings.marks: Positioning marks on the copper layer
settings.marks_hint: Two marks diagonally opposite in the margin show the position and the rotation of the panel on the mill. The lower left mark, set as close to the boards as possible, is X0 Y0 of the G-code. Needs a margin of at least 4.5 mm.
panel.marks_margin: Positioning marks need a margin of at least {min} mm.

job.marks_hint: Positioning marks: find the centre of the lower left mark (where the tips of the two quarter circles touch), set X0 Y0 there and check the centre of the upper right mark at X {x}, Y {y} mm. If it is off, the panel is turned: turn it until both fit.

job.rotation_hint: The panel is hardly ever exactly square on the mill. Set X0 Y0 at the lower left mark, move to the centre of the upper right mark and type the X and Y the control shows into the fields (they start with the place the mark should have: X {x}, Y {y} mm). Enter the result as the rotation in the control, then start the programs.
job.rotation_detail: The distance from X0 Y0 differs by {mm} mm ({percent} %). A large value means a misread position or a wrong scale.
job.rotation_invalid: Enter X and Y of the upper right mark.
series.heading: Exposure series
series.lead: A test exposure to find the right exposure time. The panel is divided into strips with the same test pattern (tracks and gaps from 0.1 to 0.5 mm, pads, SMD rows, a copper pour, small text). The panel stays on the display; every exposure lights one strip more, so the first strip gets the longest time and the last one the shortest.
series.created: {name} is saved. Copy it to the USB stick of the printer.
series.failed: The file could not be created: {message}
series.how_1: Lay a photoresist board of the panel size on the display with the copper side down, as for a normal exposure.
series.how_2: Start the file from the USB stick. The printer exposes all layers by itself; do not move the board. Between the layers it lifts the Z axis for a few seconds.
series.how_3: Develop and etch the board as usual.
series.how_4: Choose the shortest time at which the exposed areas are etched clean and the fine tracks and gaps are still sharp. Every strip shows its time; seen from the copper side the first strip (longest time) is on the left.
series.how_5: Enter this time as the exposure time in the settings of the editor.
series.leak_hint: Black areas of the display let a little UV light through. In a long series the strips with short times get a small extra dose.
series.view_label: The strips seen from the copper side
series.view_hint: Seen from the copper side. Darker strips get more light.
series.summary: {layers} layers of {unit} s each, about {time} with the lift moves between the layers.
series.err_range: Enter whole seconds from 1 to 3600 and 2 to 10 steps.
series.err_order: The longest time must be longer than the shortest.
series.err_span: {steps} steps need at least {need} seconds between the shortest and the longest time.
series.err_width: {steps} strips are {width} mm wide on this panel, the pattern needs 14 mm. Use at most {most} steps.
series.err_layers: These times need {layers} layers of {unit} s (at most {max}): the printer exposes every layer for the same time. Choose rounder values, for example times and a range that are multiples of 5 or 10 seconds.
